bluetooth_classic.notes: Classic BR/EDR only on this evidence. No BLE GATT control surface is declared. A BLE-only scanner cannot discover or drive this printer.

profiles.notes: The only printing/status channel. Pair first with Just Works, then open the authenticated SPP socket. Commands below are never sent to the three vendor SDP channels.

SDP service name Apple Inc. Required by the official app's second-generation identification and by a faithful emulator. Its payload protocol is not specified here and it is not the print path. The same UUID can appear in inquiry data, sometimes byte-reversed by the host as ffcacade-afde-cade-defa-cade00000000.
SDP service name WeChat. Present in the second-generation service set; no command protocol is claimed.
SDP service name FSK. Its 0223 UUID segment is part of the second-generation identification evidence. It is not a print channel and no firmware or other use is inferred from it.

framing.notes: Command and reply frames are exactly 34 bytes: an 8-byte header plus a 26-byte payload, with no length field or checksum. Accumulate the RFCOMM stream, discard to the next 43 F0, retain a trailing 43 while waiting for F0, and emit a reply only when all 34 bytes are present. Match the echoed command at bytes 5-6 and check error status at byte 7. The exception is the raw JPEG byte stream after a successful PRINT_READY: exactly the announced byte count is sent with no 43 0F envelope, then one 34-byte 0x0302 acknowledgement is read.

serial.notes: Strict request/response: send one 34-byte command and wait for its response before the next command. Responses typically take 0.1-0.7 s; five seconds is the public client's per-command timeout. The printer closes the link about 20 seconds after a print, so reconnect and run START_SESSION before the next operation. Multiple prints in one session are untested.

format.name: battery_voltage_raw
format.notes: High byte of the big-endian power word; raw unit and exact meaning uncertain.

format.name: error_code
format.notes: Same error-code table as get_status.error_code.

format.name: queue_status
format.notes: Same queue-state table as get_status.queue_status; this acknowledgement is not a completion event.

format.name: queue_flags
format.notes: Same bit assignments as get_status.queue_flags.

unsolicited.name: print_receive_ack
unsolicited.notes: Sent once after the last announced JPEG byte arrives. Byte 7 = 0 acknowledges receipt only. It does NOT say paper has finished printing. Poll get_status every 2-5 seconds until READY after print activity, or treat a disconnect after observed progress 100 as finished. No per-chunk acknowledgements exist.

get_info.description: GET_INFO (0x0102): read product code, Bluetooth address, serial number and PV223 model string.
get_info.notes: Owner-specific address and serial values must remain local to a client. The test vector uses a locally administered documentation address and an invented serial. The third serial character is reported to select the body-colour icon; see protocol_details.body_colour_codes.

format.name: bluetooth_address
format.notes: Six address octets, most significant first; conventionally displayed colon-separated in the same order.

format.name: serial_length
format.notes: Length n of the UTF-8 serial at payload p[7]. Model length and model follow the n serial bytes; parse dynamically using protocol_details.get_info_payload, not fixed offsets.

format.name: serial_and_model
format.notes: Remainder of the shared 26-byte payload: n serial bytes, one model-length byte m, m model bytes, then zero padding. n + m <= 18; observed serial length is 12 and model is PV223.

get_settings.description: SETTING read (0x0103, access 00): read auto-off, firmware/TMD versions, print counter and uncertain fields.

format.name: firmware_version
format.notes: Three independent bytes a b c displayed a.b.c; 01 04 0D is 1.4.13. These are version digits, not a multi-byte integer.

format.name: tmd_version
format.notes: Displayed 0.0.x in decimal; 0x18 is 0.0.24. Single byte, so no byte order applies.

format.name: photos_printed
format.notes: Lifetime printed-photo counter; blue calibration sheets are not counted.

values.0: observed value; body colour is encoded in the serial instead

format.name: settings_unknown_9_10
format.notes: Increases slowly with use; possibly a calibration counter, unconfirmed.

get_status.description: STATUS (0x0101): read battery, error, queue state, paper/cover/calibration flags and print progress.
get_status.notes: Before PRINT_READY require response_status and error_code zero, queue_status READY and flag bits 0-4 clear. A newly loaded paper pack can keep calibration bit 3 set for about 35 seconds; poll rather than print. During completion polling, READY after observed preparation or printing is the terminal success state. READY with progress 100 is also accepted by the public client; a disconnect after progress 100 can be treated as finished.

format.name: battery_voltage_raw
format.notes: High byte of big-endian power word; assumed raw battery-voltage unit, unconfirmed.

format.name: battery_percent
format.notes: Power-word bits 0-6; no additional scale.

format.name: error_code
format.notes: Idle cover/paper conditions can be flags only with this byte still zero. A paper jam is queue_status 0x10, not an error code.

values.0: READY: idle; after observed print activity, finished
values.1: PRINT_PREPARATION: preparing, also possible briefly after printing

format.name: queue_flags
format.notes: Bits 0-4 are cover open, no paper, wrong paper, Smart Sheet scanning and Smart Sheet error. Bits 5-15 are unused/unknown.

format.name: print_progress
format.notes: Signed wire byte; observed progress is 25, 50, 75, 100. It remains 100 after returning to READY.

print_ready.description: PRINT_READY (0x0301): announce the exact JPEG byte length before raw transfer; a non-zero reply refuses the print.
print_ready.example_notes: Announce 1,157,644 JPEG bytes (0x0011AA0C), copied from the public protocol's worked example and padded to 34 bytes.
print_ready.notes: Run start_session and a successful readiness check first. Only after a zero response_status write send_jpeg. The literal payload bytes p[4]=01 and p[5]=01 must not be generalised to other values without new evidence.

jpeg_size.description: Exact number of raw JPEG bytes that send_jpeg will write, encoded as one big-endian uint32 at payload p[0-3]. The two following literal 01 bytes are observed constants whose meanings (possibly copies and print mode) are unknown.

format.name: response_status
format.notes: Non-zero refuses the print; send no JPEG bytes.

format.name: battery_voltage_raw
format.notes: Raw unit, uncertain.

format.name: error_code
format.notes: Same table as get_status.error_code.

format.name: queue_status
format.notes: Same table as get_status.queue_status.

format.name: queue_flags
format.notes: Same bits as get_status.queue_flags; check bits 0-4 before transfer.

reboot.advanced_reason: Restarts the printer and drops the current session. Use only when idle; interrupting a transfer or mechanical print can waste paper and leave job state uncertain. Reconnect and run START_SESSION afterwards.
reboot.description: REBOOT (0xFFFF): restart the printer. Documented request only; no reply is established.

response.notes: The public protocol documents the request bytes but no response or post-reboot timing. Do not wait for an invented acknowledgement; reconnect and establish a fresh session.

send_jpeg.description: Raw prepared JPEG bytes following accepted PRINT_READY, in chunks no larger than the session image_chunk_size, with no framing or per-chunk acknowledgement.
send_jpeg.notes: Write chunks back to back with no delay and rely on RFCOMM flow control. Use at most image_chunk_size from START_SESSION; if it is zero/unknown, use 650 B. Zoemini 2 reports 0xFFFF, whose unlimited meaning is uncertain; the public client caps writes at 4096 B to report progress. Throughput is about 100 kB/s. Do not send another command until the receive ACK arrives.

jpeg.description: One complete baseline JFIF JPEG prepared by protocol_details.jpeg_format. Its byte length must exactly equal print_ready.jpeg_size. Maximum accepted file size is unknown; files over 1 MiB are reported accepted.

format.name: battery_voltage_raw
format.notes: Raw unit, uncertain.

response.notes: The single 0x0302 frame after the last JPEG byte is a receive acknowledgement, not print completion. Poll get_status every 2-5 seconds afterwards.

set_auto_power_off.description: SETTING write (0x0103, access 01): set the persistent auto power-off delay to 3, 5 or 10 minutes and return full settings.
set_auto_power_off.example_notes: Set auto power-off to 5 minutes. A successful reply has the get_settings layout with auto_power_off_minutes already equal to 5.
set_auto_power_off.notes: The setting persists across power cycles according to the public protocol. Verify the returned minutes byte before reporting success.

minutes.description: Delay before automatic power-off. All other payload bytes stay zero; no separate commit command is needed.

format.name: auto_power_off_minutes
format.notes: Must equal the requested value; otherwise treat the write as not applied.

format.name: firmware_version
format.notes: Three bytes a b c displayed a.b.c.

format.name: tmd_version
format.notes: Displayed 0.0.x.

response.notes: A read and a write return the same full-settings layout. Non-zero response_status means refusal; do not send image data or assume persistence.

start_session.description: START_SESSION (0x0000): open a session and return protocol byte, power word and maximum image chunk size.
start_session.notes: Unlike every other request, this uses device type FFFF and device code FF. The response power word is big-endian at frame bytes 9-10 (payload p[1-2]); low-seven-bit battery and mains bit are decoded from its low byte. Worked response in protocol_details.test_vectors.

values.1: observed value; possibly protocol version, meaning unknown

format.name: battery_voltage_raw
format.notes: High byte of power word p[1-2]; raw unit and exact meaning uncertain.

format.name: image_chunk_size
format.notes: Maximum raw JPEG chunk. Zoemini 2 reports 0xFFFF; whether that means unlimited is unknown. The public client caps writes at 4096 B for progress, or uses 650 B when no MTU is known.

class_of_device.notes: Imaging / printer, as reported by the public protocol.

methods.notes: Match the exact Mini Printer name shape AND all four SDP services. The vendor app's broader expression also recognises Instant Camera; that shape is intentionally excluded here because the camera-printer generations are not established by this evidence. SPP alone is the first-generation boundary and must not select this spec. The inquiry response can also carry the channel-22 vendor UUID, sometimes shown byte-reversed by host tooling; that display reversal is not another service. The duration of discoverability after power-on is unknown.

host_compatibility.basis: The official Android app and the public protocol use the Classic RFCOMM/SPP path with Just Works pairing. Static app analysis was used only for model scope, not to assert a different transport.
The pinned public client uses Linux RFCOMM sockets and its author reports successful Zoemini 2 printing on BlueZ 5.82. This is upstream hardware evidence, not a result reproduced by this project.

CoreBluetooth exposes no RFCOMM API, so a third-party iOS client cannot open the SPP control channel described here. Canon ships an iOS app and the printer advertises a vendor service named Apple Inc. on channel 22, but neither fact establishes an iAP2/MFi route or that the same frames are carried there. No vendor-MFi claim is made.
host_compatibility.notes: macOS is outside this verdict; its Classic stack is IOBluetooth. The iOS app's actual transport remains an open question, not a reason to mark this RFCOMM surface compatible.

identification.notes: This is a Classic-only control surface, so the inquiry name belongs to device.discovery.methods, not to BLE local-name fields. The advertised form is Canon (XX:XX) Mini Printer, where XX:XX is the last two bytes of the printer's Bluetooth address. Name alone is not a generation check: require the second-generation SDP services as well.

device.name: Canon Ivy 2 / Zoemini 2 / iNSPiC PV-223
device.notes:
Second-generation 2 x 3 inch ZINK photo printers sold as Ivy 2 in the US, Zoemini 2 in Europe and iNSPiC PV-223 in Japan. The device reports model string PV223. Control is local over Bluetooth Classic BR/EDR, not BLE: pair with Secure Simple Pairing Just Works, open RFCOMM channel 1 (SPP), then exchange strict request/response frames. No Canon account or cloud is needed by the public client.
SCOPE. This specification is ONLY for Ivy 2, Zoemini 2 and iNSPiC PV-223. PV-123, ZV-123 and ZV-223 are explicitly out of scope. In particular, an SPP-only advertisement denotes a first-generation printer with a different protocol; do not send this frame map to it. The second-generation name match must be combined with the SDP service set in device.discovery.
STREAM. Commands are 34 bytes beginning 43 0F; replies are 34 bytes beginning 43 F0. Both have an 8-byte header and a 26-byte zero-padded payload. All multi-byte integers are big-endian. There is no application checksum. Reassemble across RFCOMM reads and synchronise on 43 F0. After PRINT_READY succeeds, the announced number of raw JPEG bytes is sent with no frame envelope. The later 0x0302 acknowledgement means image receipt, not mechanical completion; poll STATUS until the queue returns to READY.
SAFETY. No firmware-update command or procedure is specified. The public protocol leaves opcodes 0x0201-0x0203 undocumented and warns against sending them. They are deliberately absent from commands and no firmware_update feature is declared.

openness.notes: Canon does not publish this local protocol. The pinned public project supplies an independent Python client, CUPS path, emulator and written protocol. Its author reports printing on Zoemini 2 hardware; this project has not repeated those tests.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The public client powers the printer on and pairs from the host; it documents no separate pairing button or hold. The exact discovery window and LED indication are not established. XX:XX is a placeholder for the final two Bluetooth-address bytes, not a literal advertised string.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app or other host, then reconnect. If pairing was forgotten on either side, remove the host's stale entry and pair again; no printer-side selective unpair procedure is documented.

pairing.notes: Basis: the pinned protocol states Secure Simple Pairing Just Works, no PIN, one host at a time, and the public client's pair-once workflow. Pairing is required by that documented flow; acceptance of an unbonded insecure socket has not been investigated and is not claimed.

unpair.clears: The bond on the host where the printer entry is removed; no printer-side selective deletion is documented.
unpair.notes: Remove the printer in the host OS Bluetooth settings and pair again when needed. This does not clear printer settings and is not a factory reset. How to delete one bond on the printer itself is unknown.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi credential, application key or account token exists in this protocol. Just Works pairing creates a Bluetooth link key but provides no PIN and no man-in-the-middle authentication. Bond storage capacity and eviction behaviour are unknown.

factory_reset.description: Basis: the pinned public protocol documents no factory reset, and the reviewed research supplies no model-matched owner procedure. Do not borrow a reset sequence from another Canon generation. Rebinding does not require one: remove the host-side bond if needed and pair again.
factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset procedure or reset command is established. Whether any physical reset clears the auto-off setting, pairing records or other persistent state is unknown; a power cycle or host-side unpair is not a factory reset.

methods.description: Power on, close any other client, identify the printer by its exact name and four-service SDP set, pair with Just Works (no PIN), then open SPP channel 1 and start a session. Basis: the pinned public protocol and client README; not replayed by this project.
methods.name: Pair in the host Bluetooth settings and open second-generation SPP

steps.action: Switch the printer on and close Canon Mini Print or any other client connected to it.
steps.expect: The printer is idle and available to one new host.

steps.action: Run a Bluetooth Classic inquiry and select Canon (XX:XX) Mini Printer only when its SDP record contains all four services declared in device.discovery.
steps.expect: A second-generation PV-223 candidate, not an SPP-only first-generation printer or an Instant Camera.

steps.action: Pair using Secure Simple Pairing Just Works; do not enter a PIN.
steps.expect: The host completes pairing without user input and may trust/store the bond for later use.

steps.action: Open RFCOMM channel 1 for SPP UUID 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.
steps.notes: Resolve the SPP record with SDP where the host requires it; the public protocol reports fixed channel 1.

steps.action: Send start_session and wait for its 34-byte reply, then send get_status before any print.
steps.expect: START_SESSION reports battery and image chunk size; STATUS is READY with no error and queue-flag bits 0-4 clear (wait if calibration bit 3 is set).

troubleshooting.fix: Only one host can connect. Close the vendor app and other clients, power-cycle if necessary, and repeat inquiry/pairing. A printer already remembered by the host can be selected from bonded devices without a new inquiry.
troubleshooting.symptom: The printer is absent or the connection times out.

troubleshooting.fix: Inspect SDP rather than overriding generation selection. An SPP-only record is outside this spec. The second-generation set includes the vendor service on channel 22 and the FSK service on channel 25 in addition to SPP and the channel-23 service.
troubleshooting.symptom: The result has the right name but is identified as a first-generation printer.

troubleshooting.fix: Remove the stale printer entry in that host's Bluetooth settings and pair again. The public client reports that a printer can forget a host after other pairings; bond capacity is unknown.
troubleshooting.symptom: A previously paired host is refused.

setup.notes: There is no Wi-Fi, account or cloud provisioning, but a Classic pairing/bond is the documented route before opening the control socket. Confidence is medium because the flow comes from the pinned public protocol and its hardware-tested client, not from a test by this project.

rejoin.notes: There is no network to rejoin. A new host pairs directly. Disconnect the old host first; if either side has a stale bond, remove the printer from that host's Bluetooth settings and pair again.

steps.action: Close the old client or disable its Bluetooth connection to the printer.
steps.expect: The single available connection is released.

steps.action: On the new host, select the printer from bonded devices or repeat the generation-checked inquiry, pair with Just Works, open SPP channel 1 and send start_session.
steps.expect: A valid START_SESSION reply establishes the new local session without a factory reset or cloud account.

testing.notes: No printer was available to this project and no new capture was made. The pinned public implementation reports successful printing and emulator use on Zoemini 2 units; those are upstream results, not tests performed from this specification.

variants.notes: US retail name in the PV-223 family. The public implementation identifies this family by GET_INFO model PV223; no Ivy-2-specific hardware capture was made for this spec.
European retail name and the variant on which the public implementation reports hardware tests. Its replies use product code 0x21.
Japanese retail name in the same PV-223 family according to the pinned public implementation. Regional behaviour has not been independently captured by this project.

entities.name: Charging
entities.notes: Power-word bit 7 means on mains / charging; it is not a separate charge-complete reading.

entities.name: Print Progress
entities.notes: Poll every 2-5 seconds after receive ACK. 100 can remain after READY; queue state determines completion.

entities.name: Reading Smart Sheet
entities.notes: Wait for this to clear after loading a new pack; it can remain set for about 35 seconds.

entities.name: Photos Printed
entities.notes: Calibration sheets are excluded from the counter.

entities.name: Firmware Version
entities.notes: Three version bytes rendered major.minor.patch in decimal; the vector 01 04 0D means 1.4.13.

initialization.notes: Must be the first application frame on every new RFCOMM connection. Retain the reported image chunk size and battery state.
Required before printing. READY, response/payload error zero and queue-flag bits 0-4 clear are the gate; poll while Smart Sheet calibration bit 3 is set.

covers: Session establishment, battery/status, identity, versions and print counter
Prepared 640 x 1608 baseline-JPEG printing with receive ACK and completion polling
not_covered: PV-123, ZV-123, ZV-223 and every SPP-only first-generation protocol
Firmware update: no safe mechanism, image mapping, signing or recovery sequence is specified
The payload protocols on RFCOMM channels 22, 23 and 25
local_access.summary: Pair directly over Classic Bluetooth and print or query status without a Canon account or cloud. The pinned public implementation provides Linux and CUPS clients; this repository supplies protocol documentation, not a supported device-client library.

body_colour_codes.description: Reported meaning of the serial string's third character (index 2), used only for display icon selection; it is not a protocol capability check.
body_colour_codes.unknown: Use a generic printer icon for any other character or a serial shorter than three characters.

error_codes.description: Response byte 7 and STATUS payload p[2] share these codes. Codes 0x1x prevent a print from starting; 0x2x occur during printing. Paper jam is queue status 0x10 instead.

out_of_scope_values.0x25: camera write error, reported for camera-printers that this spec does not cover

firmware_update.answer: No firmware-update capability is specified for a replacement client. The public protocol names 0x0201-0x0203 only as undocumented update opcodes, warns never to send them, and its emulator refuses them. No command templates, DFU entry, image format, model mapping, signature verification, bootloader identity or interrupted-update recovery are asserted here. Bundled vendor file names in research are not evidence of eligibility or a safe update route. No firmware_update feature is declared.

fields.name: device_or_product_code
fields.response: product code 20, 21 or 22 for the PV-223 family

fields.name: command
fields.response: echoed command code; 0302 for receive ACK

frame_layout.receive_rule: Accumulate across RFCOMM reads, scan to 43 F0 and take exactly 34 bytes. Preserve a trailing 43 until the next read determines whether F0 follows. Outside raw JPEG transfer, no other device-to-host frame shape is known.

get_info_payload.bounds_rule: Reject n or m whose length-prefixed strings extend past payload byte 25; never scan for a NUL terminator.
get_info_payload.description: Dynamic layout within the 26-byte payload p[]. n and m are byte lengths, strings are UTF-8 with no terminator, and unused trailing bytes are zero. n + m <= 18. The response's frame byte 4 independently carries product code.

canvas.orientation: portrait pixel array rotated 180 degrees relative to the upright source

content.physical_aspect_ratio: approximately 2:3 after accounting for non-square pixels

jpeg_format.description: The printer performs no scaling, rotation or colour processing. Prepare this exact image before print_ready; acceptance of other geometry, progressive JPEG, ICC profiles or a maximum size is not established.

encoding.maximum_bytes: unknown; files over 1 MiB are reported accepted

preparation_steps: Centre-crop the upright source to the content's physical ratio, 634 : (1596 / 1.675), approximately 2:3.
Resize to exactly 634 x 1596 without preserving the source pixel aspect ratio.
Paste at (3, 6) on a white 640 x 1608 canvas.
Remember content rows 6 and 1601, shift the whole image down 4 rows, fill rows 0-9 with remembered row 6 and rows 1604-1607 with remembered row 1601. Keep the 3 white columns at each side white.
Encode as baseline JFIF JPEG, quality 90, 4:4:4 chroma, RGB with no alpha, ICC profile or EXIF. Compute jpeg_size from the resulting encoded bytes, not the pixel count.
jpeg_format.rendering_note: Optional shadow/midtone lifting and light sharpening can improve ZINK output but are presentation choices, not protocol requirements.

completion.failure: PAPER_JAM, error codes 0x21-0x24, or timeout waiting for completion
completion.not_started: READY with progress below 100 and no observed preparation/printing is not completion; the public client fails if printing has not started after 30 seconds
completion.success: queue_status READY after observed PREPARATION/PRINTING, or READY with progress 100; disconnect after progress 100 is also accepted by the public client

ordered_steps: Connect RFCOMM channel 1 and send start_session; retain image_chunk_size.
Send get_status. Require response status and payload error zero, queue READY and flag bits 0-4 clear; poll while calibration bit 3 is set.
Send print_ready with the exact JPEG length and literal 01 01 trailing parameters. A non-zero response status refuses the job; send no image bytes.
Send exactly the announced JPEG bytes with send_jpeg, back to back in chunks no larger than image_chunk_size (650 B fallback, 4096 B public-client cap for the reported 0xFFFF MTU).
Read one print_receive_ack (0x0302). Non-zero status means image refusal; zero means received, not mechanically complete.

Poll get_status every 2-5 seconds. PREPARATION or PRINTING establishes that the print started; a later READY is successful completion. PAPER_JAM and 0x2x errors are failures; inspect TRANSIENT/RECOVERABLE error codes.

Expect the printer to close the link about 20 seconds after finishing. If it drops after observed progress 100, the public client accepts completion. Reconnect and START_SESSION for another operation.

scope.generation_rule: Require the exact Mini Printer inquiry-name shape and the four SDP services in device.discovery. SPP-only means first generation and a different protocol. The vendor app's Instant Camera name alternative is not sufficient evidence for this spec and is excluded.

product_codes.0x20: PV-223 family revision; retail-model mapping uncertain
product_codes.0x22: PV-223 family revision; retail-model mapping uncertain

sdp_generation_boundary.reject: Do not select this spec for a device publishing only SPP, and do not emulate second generation without all four SDP records.

test_vectors.description: Full 34-byte frames. start_session, status_ready, get_settings and print_ready reproduce the public protocol's worked values with zero padding made explicit. Status timeline and print_receive_ack follow the public emulator's reported state sequence. get_info is computed from the public GET_INFO layout with documentation address 02:00:00:00:00:01 and invented serial XXFTEST00001. set_auto_power_off is computed from the public write layout. None is a new hardware capture.

print_ready.meaning: Announce a 1,157,644-byte JPEG and the two observed 01 constants

reboot.meaning: Advanced REBOOT request; no reply established

start_session.meaning: START_SESSION with special FFFF/FF device selector and zero payload

get_info.meaning: Documentation address, 12-byte invented serial XXFTEST00001, five-byte model PV223, one trailing zero pad

get_settings.meaning: Auto-off 3 min, firmware 1.4.13, unknown byte 5, TMD 0.0.24, 11 photos, colour id 0, unknown word 2

print_receive_ack.meaning: Image accepted with idle status; still not mechanical completion

start_session.meaning: Product 0x21, session byte 1, power 0x8264 = battery 100% on battery, raw high byte 0x82, MTU 0xFFFF

status_preparing_25.meaning: Print preparation, 25%: print has started but is not complete

status_ready.meaning: Power 0x81E4 = mains/charging and battery 100%, READY, no errors or flags, progress 0

status_ready_complete.meaning: READY with progress 100 after print activity: completion

remaining_unknowns: One owner-controlled SDP/frame capture per regional PV-223 retail variant is still needed; upstream hardware results are Zoemini 2 results, not proof for every alias.
Which retail revisions correspond to product codes 0x20 and 0x22; only Zoemini 2's 0x21 mapping is reported.
PV-123, ZV-123 and ZV-223 protocols and compatibility are unestablished and deliberately excluded; SPP-only first-generation devices need a separate capture.
START_SESSION p[0] (observed 1), the power word's high-byte raw unit, PRINT_READY's two 01 constants, SETTING p[4] and p[9-10], and queue-flag bits 5-15.
Whether MTU 0xFFFF literally means unlimited; the public client caps writes at 4096 B. Maximum accepted JPEG size and acceptance of progressive JPEG, other dimensions or ICC profiles are unknown.
Several prints in one session without reconnecting, low-battery behaviour, and opening the cover during a print are untested upstream.
Factory-reset existence/effect, pairing-window indication, bond capacity and printer-side selective unpairing.
How the official iOS app reaches the printer; channel 22's presence and Apple Inc. service name do not establish MFi/iAP2 or frame compatibility.
Firmware update: no safe commands, image-to-model mapping, signing, bootloader state or recovery is specified. Do not send 0x0201-0x0203; no firmware_update feature is declared.
No model-matched official PV-223 manual or FCC ID was established by the research.
